observation: The whole set, opening position, all 182 occurrences. Top view: the 7x9 field is correct -- twelve cocoa-brown belt tiles in two 2x3 blocks on files b-c and e-f across ranks 4-6, the Sol star at d1 with its three orange corona cells at c1, d2 and e1, the Anti-Sol star at d9 with three cyan cells at c9, d8 and e9, and sixteen pieces on their opening cells, eight on white discs and eight on black. Both trays sit clear of the board with eight sockets each, one per captured world. Iso view: the rank ladder reads at a glance -- Mercury is the smallest ball and Jupiter and Saturn the largest -- and Saturn's ring and its support web are present on both armies, mirrored. Front view: every piece stands on the board plane, disc walls draft outward on the white army and inward on the black, and the two star flames rise clear and lean outward. Nothing floats, nothing is missing, no part is duplicated, and no intersection is visible. Three things a reader of these images could mistake for faults were each measured rather than eyeballed and are not faults: the star flames and corona tongues stand beside a seated world and never inside one (measure/seated-piece-clearance.md, 0.000000 mm3 shared for all eight worlds at both seats); the ring meets the disc across a shared surface by design, not an overlap (inspect interfere reports clashCount 0 on the whole assembly); and the den flange is exactly one cell pitch, so it abuts its neighbours rather than overhanging them. The renderer's own limits are visible and are not geometry: black discs come out as flat silhouettes with no top face, the trays read as floating because no ground plane or shadow is drawn, and the numerals face the two seated players so they are nearly side-on at this camera.
